newsletter.subject: The Security Diff — November 15, 2026
newsletter.preview_text: CI credentials, trusted releases and forgotten cloud access: three incidents, three patch briefings and one agent-security research note.

stories.title: wfx-loot turns stolen GitHub access into CI credential theft
stories.summary: Aikido reports stolen GitHub credentials were used to inject secret-stealing workflows and install hooks into repositories from November 10. Probe pull requests do not prove every repository executed the payload; deleted run logs can hide execution.
stories.why_it_matters: A CI compromise can expose workflow secrets, cloud identities and publishing access. A clean current branch does not establish that earlier runs were clean.
stories.action: Audit suspicious branches, workflow history and OIDC changes. If the payload ran, treat workflow-accessible credentials as exposed and investigate persistence before restoring trust.

stories.title: Malicious bee-js and Swarm Desktop releases abuse a trusted release path
stories.summary: Socket and SafeDep report malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 releases delivering remote-code loaders. The npm package carried valid provenance; affected systems need compromise assessment, not just a package downgrade.
stories.why_it_matters: Release provenance can faithfully attest to malicious code built through a compromised workflow. Swarm node wallet keys and persistent backdoors are part of the reported impact.
stories.action: Check install and launcher history. Isolate affected systems, rotate exposed credentials from a clean machine, and follow the researchers’ wallet-key and persistence-removal guidance.

stories.title: Qubole-linked credentials expose forgotten AWS integration roles
stories.summary: Wiz and Sentra’s November 9 disclosures describe attackers using Qubole-associated AWS credentials to assume customer integration roles, collect secrets and access S3 data. Wiz dates the observed activity to October 14–26; this is a new disclosure of older activity.
stories.why_it_matters: Dormant vendor trust can remain usable after an integration stops being used. An External ID did not prevent the observed role assumptions.
stories.action: Inventory and remove unused vendor trusts. Review unusual role assumptions and S3 object reads, limit integration-role permissions, and investigate exposed secrets.

stories.title: Apache HTTP/2 flaw makes exposure checks and patching urgent
stories.summary: Apache identifies CVE-2026-119618 in mod_http2, affecting HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70. The fix shipped in 2.4.71 on November 11. This is a disclosed RCE vulnerability; Aikido reported no known in-the-wild exploitation as of November 13.
stories.why_it_matters: HTTP/2 configuration and the protocol reaching the backend determine exposure. A version match or a vendor’s cloud prevalence percentage does not establish an exploitable deployment.
stories.action: Apply Apache 2.4.71 or a vendor-confirmed backport. If patching must wait, review disabling HTTP/2 and verify that the backend no longer accepts it.

stories.title: MongoDB catch-up flaw reaches replica sets before authentication
stories.summary: MongoDB disclosed CVE-2026-118383 on November 10. The replication use-after-free affects replica set members, including shard and config-server members; standalone instances are outside its scope. Datadog reproduced a crash, while the advisory also describes possible code execution.
stories.why_it_matters: Authentication alone does not stop the triggering requests. The catch-up condition matters; a reproduced crash does not prove reliable RCE or attacks in the wild.
stories.action: Upgrade every affected replica set member to its branch’s fixed release. Datadog lists 8.0.37 for the 8.0 branch; restrict network access while completing the rollout.

stories.title: Node.js security updates address HTTP/2 crashes and memory disclosure
stories.summary: The Node.js November 11 security release fixes HTTP/2 denial-of-service and memory-disclosure issues, an HTTPS parser re-entrancy flaw, and other bugs. The project provides 22.23.5, 24.22.3 and 26.13.1; affected release lines and trigger conditions vary by issue.
stories.why_it_matters: Applications serving HTTP/2 or handling the affected HTTPS patterns need runtime updates. Updating application dependencies alone does not replace the Node.js runtime.
stories.action: Move to the security release for your supported Node.js line, rebuild deployed images and check running versions. Consult the upstream per-issue scope before claiming a deployment is unaffected.

stories.title: Research: coding-agent backdoors can survive ordinary evaluation
stories.summary: Microsoft’s November 12 research demonstrates poisoned fine-tuning data and backdoored checkpoints causing coding agents to misuse tools. These are controlled studies, not a disclosed customer breach. Dataset governance, checkpoint provenance and tool permissions remain separate controls.
stories.why_it_matters: Training-data integrity, checkpoint provenance and runtime tool permissions address different trust boundaries in these controlled studies.
stories.action: Pin and review training inputs, evaluate the exact deployed agent configuration, and restrict tool permissions and credentials outside the model.

sources.name: Microsoft Security Research and AI Red Team

signal.label: recommended
reasons: Reviewed editorial selection: 9/10; this is not a vulnerability score.
